items.note: By Bhoja's orders the sculptor Manathala executed an image of Sarasvati in Sam 1091 = 1034 AD (now in the British Museum), as a sign of high iconography in Bhoja's time.
Image of a goddess found in the Devi tank at Dhar, pedestal inscription dated Sam 1138 = 1081 AD, within Udayaditya's reign.
The Udayapur prasasti attributes the erection of a number of pillars of victory to Vairisimha II; the Dhar iron pillar may be his work.
Paramara kings described as votaries of the Goddess of learning, many themselves poets, encouraging others.
The Udayapur prasasti says Vakpatiraja cultivated eloquence, lofty poetry, the art of reasoning and mastery of the Sastras.
Muñja's reported exclamation on being led to execution: when Muñja has passed away, Sarasvati will be without support.
Ain-i-Akbari on Bhoja honouring wisdom, with five hundred sages at his court.
The Udayapur prasasti glorifies Bhoja as the king of poets.
Samaranganasutradhara (Architecture) appears in the list of works ascribed to Bhoja.
Doubt whether Bhoja himself wrote so many books; some seem written by literary men under his guidance.
Udayaditya and Naravarman staunch supporters of cultural movements; Naravarman a poet who composed the Nagpur prasasti.
The Kamalmauka mosque at Dhara believed a school built by Bhoja; two charts on its walls with alphabets and grammar rules corroborate the tradition.
First chart: single serpent with Sanskrit alphabet in Nagari characters of the 11th-12th centuries; tail holds inflectional terminations.
Second chart: two intertwined serpents recording Ka-tantra grammar rules; similar charts at the Mahakala temple at Ujjain and at a fane at Un.
Dhanapala migrated to Dhara, studied Brahmanic learning, gained Bhoja's notice and rose to be a principal court poet.
Merutunga's story of Bhoja burning Dhanapala's Tilakamanjari manuscript, reproduced by his daughter; the author notes there is no corroborating evidence.
Dhanika, in Paramara administrative service, wrote the Dasarupavaloka commentary showing high literary attainments.

items.note: Padmagupta, court poet of Vakpati-Munja and Sindhuraja, composed the Navasahasanka-carita at Sindhuraja's order.
Halayudha migrated to Malava and lived at Dhara at Munja's court, praising the king's liberality.
Amitagati completed the Subhasita-ratna-samdoha in Sam 1050 = 993 AD while Munja was ruling.
Uvata settled in Avanti in the first half of the 11th century and composed the Mantrabhashya during Bhoja's reign.
Asadhara migrated to Malava in 1192, contemporary of Vindhyavarman to Jaitugideva; Nalakachapura chief centre of his teaching.
Asadhara's Trisastismrti written in Sam 1292 = 1235 AD under Devapala; Bhavyakumudacandrika in Sam 1300 = 1243 AD under Jaitugideva.
Madana, royal preceptor under Arjunavarman, composed the drama Parijata-manjari and three inscriptions of Arjunavarman's reign.

reject_reason: Jaina teacher Devendra and his works list; no bearing on any unit

items.note: Architecture reached a high pitch of excellence; the temples of Udayapur and of Un rank high among the best specimens of ancient Indian architecture.
Malwa's highest credit lies in contributions to Sanskrit literature, the crucial test of culture.
Vakpati-Munja established three new settlements at Jalor, Bhinmal and Mount Abu, appointing princes of his family as governors.
Dhandhuka of Abu a contemporary of Bhoja, during whose reign enmity between Anhilwar and Dhara became acute.
Purnapala probably with Bhoja's assistance re-established his authority over Arbudamandala.

items.note: Death of Bhoja about 1055 AD deprived the Abu princes of a strong supporter; the Paramara government was then under stress and Bhima again attacked Abu.
